another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 6 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with him and are you the person who looks after him (providing food, clothing, housing, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me currently. But I do contribute to his upkeep - I help out financially with things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

**Could you tell me who Alex lives with?** For example, does he live with his other parent, another family member, or someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. So Alex lives with his mum, your ex-partner.

**Is his mum claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** And also, **do you pay maintenance or child support for Alex, either through a formal arrangement or informally?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if she's claiming Child Benefit for him or not. But yes, I do help out financially - I contribute money regularly towards his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to clarify a bit more about your situation:

**You mentioned you contribute money regularly towards Alex's costs. Is this through a formal child maintenance arrangement (such as through the Child Maintenance Service), or is it an informal arrangement between you and his mum?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's an informal arrangement between us. I just send her money regularly to help with his clothes, food, and other things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Child Benefit is paid to the person who is **responsible for the child** - this means the person who the child lives with and who is their main carer. Since Alex lives with his mum and she is the one looking after him on a day-to-day basis (providing his home, food, clothing, etc.), she would be the person who can claim Child Benefit for him.

While it's great that you contribute financially to Alex's upkeep through informal maintenance payments, this alone doesn't make you eligible for Child Benefit. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, and that person must be the one the child lives with.

If Alex's mum isn't currently claiming Child Benefit for him, she may want to look into making a claim herself, as she would likely be eligible.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this?
